toc.title: What the Guide Says, and What It Leaves to the Objectives
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1What the Guide Says, and What It Leaves to the Objectives

The Guide gives the Scrum Master these related duties:

Where Wording
Serving the team "Coaching the team members in self-management and cross-functionality" and "ensuring that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox"
Serving the Product Owner "Facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed"
Serving the organization "Leading, training, and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption"

It does not define facilitation, teaching, mentoring or coaching. The learning objectives ask you to recognize the difference and to use each well. The four differ in who holds the answers and who does most of the thinking.

Old wording

The 2017 Guide had the Scrum Master "facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed" (for both the Product Owner and the Development Team), "coaching the Development Team in self-organization", and "coaching the Development Team in organizational environments in which Scrum is not yet fully adopted". The 2020 Guide keeps coaching, adds training and leading, and says the Scrum Master ensures that events take place and are positive, productive and timeboxed. Facilitation remains a skill, but it is no longer a duty to run every event.

2Facilitation (CSM 2.1)Beyond the Guide

A facilitator helps a group reach its own outcome. A common definition: "someone who helps a group of people understand their common objectives and assists them to plan how to achieve these objectives; in doing so, the facilitator remains 'neutral', meaning he/she doesn't take a particular position in the discussion."

The facilitator Does Does not
Process Sets the purpose, the structure, the time and the ground rules; keeps the conversation on track; makes sure everyone is heard Decide for the group
Content Stays neutral: does not push a position Argue for a solution or take sides
Outcome Helps the group make its own decision and record actions Take notes only, or lecture

Facilitation is not only for events: it is a way of helping a group collaborate anywhere.

2.1 Situations where the Scrum Master facilitates (list at least three)

Situation What facilitation looks like
Sprint Retrospective Structure the session so that everyone contributes, steer toward concrete improvements, keep it positive and productive
Sprint Planning and Sprint Goal Help the Scrum Team collaborate on a single, clear Sprint Goal
Product Backlog refinement Help the Product Owner and Developers reach a shared understanding of items
Stakeholder collaboration (the Guide's wording) Help the Product Owner and stakeholders talk to each other, for example in a Sprint Review or a workshop
Team decisions Help the Developers choose between options, for example a tool or a working agreement
Creating or improving the Definition of Done Help the Scrum Team agree on quality criteria
Conflict Help people in disagreement talk it through and find their own way forward
Sessions with managers or other teams Help the organization work through an impediment or a Scrum adoption question
Exam angle

a facilitator is neutral on content and active on process. The Scrum Master who decides for the team, argues for a favourite option, or merely takes the minutes is not facilitating. The Product Owner still decides the order of the Product Backlog and the Developers decide how, whatever the facilitation.

3Techniques for Group Decision Making (CSM 2.2)Beyond the Guide

Technique How it works Best used when Watch out for
Dot voting Each person receives the same number of dots and places them on the options they prefer; the top vote-getters win Selecting several options from a longer list, for example the improvements to try after a Retrospective Dots can be spread thin; agree on the number of dots first
Roman voting (thumbs) Each person shows a thumb up (agree), sideways (neutral, can live with it) or down (concern) A quick check on one proposal, or choosing one option Little nuance; quiet people may follow the group
Fist of Five Each person shows a number of fingers, from a closed fist (block, no support) up to five fingers (full support). Agree beforehand on the required level (for example at least three, or four for high-impact choices) Gauging the strength of support for one proposal, with more nuance than thumbs People below the level state their concerns, then the group adjusts the proposal and votes again
1-2-4-All Each person thinks alone, then talks in pairs, then in fours, then the whole group shares Important decisions when the group is far from agreement, and so that everyone contributes Needs more time
Consensus and the gradient of agreement The group seeks agreement that everyone can live with; the level of agreement required is set beforehand and can be lowered if needed Decisions that everyone must support in practice Slow; can drift into compromise or never end
Majority vote The option with more than half of the votes wins Low-impact or urgent choices The minority may disengage; use only for the team's own decisions

3.1 Choosing a technique

Need Technique
Pick several items from a list Dot voting
Quick yes or no Roman voting
How strongly does the group support it? Fist of Five
Hard topic, or the group is far from agreement 1-2-4-All, then a vote
Everyone must be able to live with it Consensus with an agreed threshold
Small, low-impact choice Majority vote

3.2 Principles for any technique

  • Agree on the method and the threshold before voting.
  • Make sure everyone understands the proposal first.
  • Use the techniques for the team's own decisions. The Product Owner remains the one who decides the order of the Product Backlog (stakeholders and the team inform it), and the Developers decide how to build.
  • A decision is only the start: record it, assign actions and check later.

4Facilitating, Teaching, Mentoring and Coaching (CSM 2.3)Beyond the Guide

Teaching Mentoring Coaching Facilitating
Short definition Helping others learn new things: imparting knowledge or skills, showing how A wise and trusted counsellor who shares experience Unlocking a person's or team's potential to maximize its own performance; helping people learn rather than teaching them Helping a group reach its objective while staying neutral on content
Who holds the answer The Scrum Master The Scrum Master (experience) The coachee The group
Scrum Master's role Explains, demonstrates, instructs Shares experience and options, advises Asks questions, listens, reflects back; does not give the answer Sets the stage, structures the process, keeps boundaries
Direction Telling and showing Sharing and advising Asking and drawing out Guiding the process
Focus Knowledge and skills Growth through experience Mindset, behaviour and self-discovery Collaboration and decisions
Typical phrase "This is how Scrum defines the Definition of Done." "When I faced this, I tried ... and learned ..." "What have you tried? What would you like to happen?" "Let us agree how we decide this. Everyone gets one minute first."
Example Explaining the Sprint rules to a new Developer Sharing own experience of splitting large Product Backlog items with a Product Owner Helping a Developer find her own way to give feedback Running a Retrospective or a decision session
Needs subject expertise? Yes Yes, in depth Not necessarily (it can even be a pitfall) No (content neutral)

4.1 Which stance to use Beyond the Guide

The situation The best stance
The team does not know a rule or a practice Teach
A person wants to learn from someone who has been there Mentor
The person or team has the ability but is stuck, or needs to find its own answer Coach
The group has to collaborate or decide Facilitate

A Scrum Master moves between stances as the situation requires: teach a new team the rules, coach a Developer to find a solution, facilitate the Retrospective, mentor a new Product Owner.

Exam angle

the test is "who has the answer?" If the Scrum Master gives knowledge or advice it is teaching or mentoring; if the Scrum Master draws the answer out it is coaching; if the Scrum Master runs the process while staying out of the content it is facilitating. Coaching is the default for self-management (the Guide's wording). Teaching is right when the problem is lack of knowledge of Scrum.

5Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. Facilitation is neutral. The facilitator does not decide or advocate for an option.
  2. Facilitation is not "taking notes" or "scheduling", and not only for Scrum events.
  3. Coaching does not give the answer. Questions, listening and reflection draw it out.
  4. Teaching imparts knowledge. When the team lacks knowledge of Scrum, teaching is the right stance.
  5. Mentoring shares experience. It requires real experience in the subject.
  6. Match the technique to the need: dot voting for several items, Roman voting for a quick check, Fist of Five for the strength of support, 1-2-4-All for hard topics.
  7. Agree the threshold before voting (for example for Fist of Five).
  8. Techniques do not move accountability. The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog; the Developers decide how.
  9. Scrum Master "decides for the team to save time" is the typical wrong answer. The best answer helps the team decide.
  10. Old wording "Facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed" is a 2017 duty. In 2020 the Scrum Master ensures events take place and are positive, productive and timeboxed.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1The Developers cannot decide between two tools and the discussion has gone in circles. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AFacilitate a quick technique such as Fist of Five with an agreed level of support, so the Developers decide
  • BChoose the tool and tell the team, as a quick decision by the Scrum Master saves the time of the whole team
  • CAsk the Product Owner to choose the tool, since the Product Owner is accountable for the value and the budget of the product
  • DPostpone the decision to the next Sprint, when the Developers may have more information about both tools
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Scrum Master facilitates: helps the group decide, stays neutral on the content and agrees on the method and threshold first. The Developers decide how to do their work, so the Scrum Master and Product Owner do not choose for them.

S2The Retrospective produced twenty improvement ideas, and the team wants to pick the few to try next Sprint. Which technique fits best?

  • ARoman voting on each of the twenty ideas in turn, so that every idea gets a thumbs up, sideways or down
  • BThe Scrum Master picks the five ideas that look most useful, to save the time of the whole team
  • CConsensus on all twenty ideas, so that everyone in the team can live with every single improvement
  • DDot voting, with each person placing a few dots, so that the top vote-getters are chosen
Show the answer

Answer: D. Dot voting is suited to selecting several options from a longer list. Roman voting on twenty ideas is slow, and consensus on all of them is unnecessary. The Scrum Master facilitates the choice but does not pick.

S3A newly hired Developer does not know what the Definition of Done is or why it matters. Which approach by the Scrum Master is best?

  • ATeach: explain the Definition of Done, show the team's own, and check understanding
  • BCoach with questions only, without any explanation
  • CAsk the Developer to read the whole Guide alone
  • DMentor the Developer by sharing stories
Show the answer

Answer: A. The need is knowledge of Scrum, which teaching addresses directly: explaining and demonstrating. Coaching works best when the person already has the ability or the answer inside, and a story does not replace the rule.

S4A new Product Owner asks the Scrum Master, who has served several Product Owners, how they handled stakeholder conflicts. Which stance is the Scrum Master taking by sharing experience and options?

  • ACoaching
  • BFacilitating
  • CMentoring
  • DTeaching the Guide
Show the answer

Answer: C. Mentoring is the stance in which the Scrum Master shares experience and possible answers. Coaching would draw the answer out of the Product Owner, and facilitating would structure a group conversation.

S5A Developer says: "I always get into arguments with a teammate and do not know what to do." The Scrum Master wants the Developer to find a way forward. Which approach is best?

  • ATell the Developer exactly what to say and do in the next argument, so that the conflict stops quickly
  • BCoach: ask what the Developer has tried, what outcome the Developer wants and which options exist
  • CMove the Developer to another team, so that the two people no longer have to work together every day
  • DIgnore it until the Retrospective, as conflicts between team members usually solve themselves over time
Show the answer

Answer: B. Coaching helps a person find their own answers with questions and reflection, especially for behaviour and mindset. Telling, moving the person or waiting do not build the Developer's own capability.

S6The Product Owner and two stakeholders disagree about priorities in a workshop. Which behaviour of the Scrum Master is correct?

  • AArgue for the Scrum Master's preferred priorities, because the Scrum Master has the best view of the whole product
  • BDecide the order of the Product Backlog, to end the disagreement quickly and let the work continue
  • CStay silent and let the stakeholders and the Product Owner settle it among themselves, whatever the result
  • DFacilitate neutrally, helping everyone be heard, while the Product Owner decides the order
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Scrum Master facilitates stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed. A facilitator is neutral on content, and the Product Owner remains accountable for ordering the Product Backlog.

S7During a facilitated decision, the Scrum Master keeps arguing for one option. What is the issue?

  • AThe Scrum Master has stopped being a neutral facilitator
  • BNothing: facilitators should argue
  • CThe technique was wrong
  • DThe Developers should vote again
Show the answer

Answer: A. A facilitator remains neutral on the content of the discussion, supports everyone to give their best thinking and helps the group reach its own decision. Advocating one option distorts the process.

S8Which technique is best for gauging how strongly a group supports one proposal, with more nuance than a thumbs vote?

  • ADot voting
  • BMajority vote
  • CFist of Five
  • D1-2-4-All
Show the answer

Answer: C. In Fist of Five each person shows from a closed fist (block) up to five fingers (full support), after the group has agreed on the level of support required. Dot voting selects among options, and 1-2-4-All is for important decisions far from agreement.

S9In a Fist of Five the team agreed beforehand that at least three fingers from everyone are required. Two members show two fingers. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • ADeclare the proposal approved because most showed more
  • BAsk those two to state their concerns, help the group adapt the proposal, and vote again
  • CRemove the two members from the decision
  • DAsk the Product Owner to decide
Show the answer

Answer: B. The required level was agreed in advance, so the group addresses the concerns of those below it and votes again. This is how the technique builds real support.

S10Which statement best distinguishes coaching from mentoring?

  • AThey are the same: both mean giving the other person advice about what to do in a given situation
  • BIn mentoring the mentor only asks questions, while a coach shares experience and answers directly
  • CCoaching always requires deep expertise in the subject, while mentoring requires only good listening skills
  • DA coach helps the coachee find their own answers; a mentor shares experience and possible answers
Show the answer

Answer: D. Coaching unlocks a person's own potential and draws out answers, and the coach need not be a subject expert. Mentoring is relational and based on the mentor's experience, which the mentor may share.

6.2 Recall Q&As

R1What does the Guide say the Scrum Master does with the Scrum Team as regards self-management?

Show the answer

Coaches the team members in self-management and cross-functionality.

R2What does the Guide say about stakeholder collaboration?

Show the answer

The Scrum Master facilitates stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed.

R3What does the Guide say about the organization?

Show the answer

The Scrum Master leads, trains and coaches the organization in its Scrum adoption.

R4What is a facilitator?

Show the answer

Someone who helps a group understand its common objectives and plan how to achieve them, while staying neutral on the content.

R5Give three situations in which the Scrum Master facilitates.

Show the answer

Sprint Retrospective; Sprint Planning and the Sprint Goal; Product Backlog refinement; stakeholder collaboration; team decisions; Definition of Done workshops; conflict; sessions with managers.

R6Name three techniques for group decision making.

Show the answer

Dot voting, Roman voting, Fist of Five, 1-2-4-All, consensus with a gradient of agreement, majority vote.

R7When is dot voting used?

Show the answer

To select several options from a longer list.

R8How does Fist of Five work?

Show the answer

Each person shows from a closed fist to five fingers to show support; the group agrees on the required level beforehand and addresses concerns of those below it.

R9What is Roman voting?

Show the answer

Thumbs up, sideways or down to approve, accept or object to a proposal.

R10What is teaching?

Show the answer

Helping others learn new things by imparting knowledge or skills and showing how.

R11What is mentoring?

Show the answer

A wise, trusted counsellor sharing their experience and possible answers.

R12What is coaching?

Show the answer

Unlocking a person's or team's potential by helping them learn and find their own answers; asking rather than telling.

R13Who holds the answer in each stance?

Show the answer

Teaching and mentoring: the Scrum Master. Coaching: the coachee. Facilitating: the group.

R14Which stance addresses a lack of Scrum knowledge?

Show the answer

Teaching.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Guide wording Coaching in self-management and cross-functionality · facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed · leading, training and coaching the organization
Facilitating Neutral on content, active on process; the group decides

Dot voting Several options from a list
Roman voting Quick thumbs check
Fist of Five Strength of support; agree the level first
1-2-4-All Hard topics; alone, pairs, fours, all
Consensus / gradient of agreement Everyone can live with it; set the level first
Majority vote Low-impact choices
Teaching Imparts knowledge; the Scrum Master holds the answer
Mentoring Shares experience and options
Coaching Asks, draws out; the coachee holds the answer
